analysis: Both changed files are test-only (libs/darkbloom-cluster/Tests/DarkbloomClusterRuntimeTests). Gemma4TensorParallelRuntimeTests.swift: the layer-stride test now uses withLayerStride(...) instead of the TaskLocal $layerStride.withValue and adds a scope test (lines 119-128). It adds strides 1, 2, 5 and 8 and checks bench-mode applicability for full, shard and tp, and refuses simulated and split-sum. It also adds request-loop cases with build-ahead (buildsAhead LoopCase field, lines 387-388, 420-421; tests at 494-537). These check that tokens, finish and logprobs are identical between build-ahead and read-then-build orders, including owner-stop races. IndependentHistoryBatchDriverTestSupport.swift: the finishGeneration test double now allows more than one discarded forward under client stop (aheadDiscardLimit) and one discard after EOS, and still checks lastTokenID and selectedTokenCount against history. This only relaxes a test assertion; it ships no production code. No production trust boundary, key handling, attestation, authorization, encryption or prefix-cache storage code (T-041) is touched. Nothing in the tests adds secrets or network surface. Remaining question for integration: the production changes behind withLayerStride, benchLayerStrideApplies and the build-ahead driver, which are not in this batch. If a client stop discards extra tokens or steps, they must never be published or leaked. Check that discarded or held tokens stay unpublished after a client stop (T-010 and T-008 area), and that cancellation still stops in-flight work. The test relaxation could mask a regression there if the production bound is wrong. This cannot be judged from the supplied test-only evidence.
